plan.english: Master, what is the sun? The sun is the eye of Sky. Does it see us? It sees us, and it sees the cattle. On what does it go? It goes on its own wheel. Who draws the wheel of the sun? Swift horses draw it. When it is getting dark, where does the sun sink? It sinks in the sea. And who leads it again? Dawn, the daughter of Sky, leads it. Does it warm the earth? It warms her. Son, keep looking at the sun. It does not stand; it goes. Day follows night, and night follows day.

When it has dawned, master, where is the night gone? Dear one, it is gone below, in the earth. And where are the stars gone? They are gone; the light of day overcame them. Does the night come again? It comes again. When the sun sinks, night comes. What does it bring? It brings sleep and cold. Who is awake? The dog and the shepherd are awake. The wolf walks. Who is afraid? The sheep are afraid. And what are Night and Dawn? They are two sisters. When night goes away, dawn comes; when dawn goes away, night comes.

Master, who holds up the sky? A great tree holds up the sky. Where does the tree stand? In the broad earth it stands. And what holds up the earth? Nothing holds it up; it is stretched out. Does the sky fall down? It does not fall down; it is stretched out above. Who placed the sky above? The first gods placed it above. The sky is our father, and the earth is our mother.

Master, who gives water to the earth? Sky gives water to the earth. And how does he give it? A serpent lay on the hill and seized the water. Were the cattle thirsty? They were thirsty, and the earth dried up. Then Perkwunos slew the serpent. Where does the serpent lie? On the hill he lies, and he does not stand up. Then the water came forth, and it rained. Who drank the water? The earth drank it. When it rains, the earth drinks, and the sheep live, and the grain grows.

Famous one, what is winter? Winter is the time of cold. What comes from the sky in winter? Snow comes from the sky. Where do the cattle stand in winter? They stand in the cow-stall. And the fire burns in the household. What do we do in winter? We sit near the fire, and we eat grain. When the sun has become strong, does the snow melt? It melts, and it becomes water. Where does the water go? The water goes to the sea. Then the days become long. Winter comes, and winter goes; the earth stands.

title: The Sea That Is Not Full

plan.english: Master, many currents go to the sea. How does the sea not become full? It does not become full. The sun drinks the water of the sea. And where does the water go? It goes up to the sky. Then it rains, and the water goes again to it. Is the sea deep? It is deep and broad. No one sees the bottom of the sea. Who put this in order? The gods put it in order.

Father, where is Fire born? Three are the births of Fire. In the sky he is born; in the water he is born; in the tree he is born. I saw Fire in the tree. How does he come forth from it? When Perkwunos strikes down the tree, Fire comes forth. What does Fire eat? He eats the tree. What kills him? Water kills him. Who guards the fire in the household? The mistress of the household guards it. He is dear to us.

Lord, how is the earth our mother? The earth nourishes us. Mother Earth nourishes the horses and the cattle. And who nourishes the earth? The sun and the water nourish her. What does the earth carry? She carries the hills, the trees and us. Does the earth become tired? She does not become tired. The plough splits the earth, and the earth gives us grain. Who guards the earth? The gods guard her. Broad is the earth, and deep.

Master, who are the gods? The gods are heavenly. Where do they dwell? In the sky they dwell. Are they many? They are many. Who is the first of them? Sky is the first of the gods. What do they give us? They give us good things. They are givers of good things. Whom do they come to love? The one who speaks the truth, him they come to love. Are the gods men? They are not. Men die; the gods do not die. Listen, son. They see us, and they hear us.

Great one, what did Sky give us? Sky gave us the day. And what does Mother Earth give us? She gives us grain and wine. And what does Dawn give us? She gives us light. Who gave us sleep? Night gave us sleep. What shall we give the gods? Give them a true word, and give them poured water. The one who gives to them, to him the gods give. Giving is dear to the gods.

Master, with what shall we call upon the gods? Call upon them with a true word. Do not call upon them with a lie. Whom do the gods listen to? The one who calls upon them with a true word, him they listen to. Where shall we stand? Stand near the fire, and be turned towards them. What shall we say to them? Say the famous names of the gods. Then ask. They hear it from the heart. They come to the household, and they sit down.

Master, who is Sky? Sky is the father of gods and men. What does he see? He sees us, and he sees the gods. Where does he sit? He sits above. Is the earth the wife of Sky? She is his wife, and he is her husband. Does he cover the earth? He covers her. Whose daughter is Dawn? Dawn is the daughter of Sky. Dear one, call upon Sky. Father Sky, hear us! May Sky hear you.

Famous one, who is Perkwunos? Perkwunos is the striker. He is strong. Where does he dwell? He dwells on the hill. Whom does he strike down? Perkwunos strikes down the serpent and the wolf. And whom does he not kill? The one who does not deceive, him he does not kill. When Perkwunos comes, do we tremble in fear? We tremble in fear, and the cattle tremble in fear. The one who knows the truth does not fear. Do not tremble in fear, dear friend.

Lord, how does the poured water arrive at the gods? Fire carries it to them. And who is Fire? He is the mouth of the gods. Through him the gods eat. What do we give him? We give him wine and grain. Where does he sit? He sits in the household. He is a guest in the household. Call upon Fire.

Father, who is Dawn? Dawn is the daughter of Sky. Is she red? She is red. What does she bring? She brings light and day. I want to see Dawn. Wake up, daughter. When it dawns, you will see her. Who catches sight of her? The one who is awake, he catches sight of her. I woke up, and I saw her; she was red. When it dawns, we wake up.

Lord, I have heard of the two sons of Sky. What do they do? They drive swift horses. How do they come? They come in a chariot. When it dawns, they come. Whom do they protect? They protect the men in the boat. When the boat sinks, they come. Where do they dwell? In the sky they dwell. May they protect you.

Great one, what is the truth? The truth is that which is. And what is the lie? The lie is that which is not. Who knows the truth? The one who has seen it, he knows. Who speaks the truth? The one who knows, he speaks the truth. With what do we get to know the truth? We get to know the truth with the eyes and the mind. The truth stands; the lie falls.

Famous one, who guards the oath? The gods guard it. Where does the oath dwell? In the heart it dwells. Whom does Perkwunos strike down? The one who breaks the oath, him Perkwunos strikes down. And whom do the gods protect? The one who guards the oath, him the gods protect. Does a man deceive them? He does not deceive them. They see the mind of man. I shall speak the truth. They are listening.

Lord, who is a guest? The one who arrives at another's household, he is a guest. What shall we give the guest? Seat him, and give him water. Where does the guest sit? Near the fire he sits. When he is sated, let him go. What does the guest carry? He carries a word from another's household. Who protects the guest? Sky protects him. Do not drive the guest away. Yesterday a guest arrived at our household. I seated him. You did right, dear one. A guest is dear to Sky.

Famous one, who steals? The one who seizes another's cattle, he steals. Does the man who steals walk by night? He walks, and he fears the light. What does he steal? He steals silver and sheep. Who sees him? The dog sees him. What shall the man who steals give? Whoever steals cattle, let him give them back twice. Does the one who moves the boundary of another's field steal? He does indeed steal. Another's cattle are not one's own.

Master, what is right? The right is that which the king sets upright. How does he set it upright? The carpenter straightens the tree; the king straightens us. And who makes the king straight? The gods make him straight. Who goes astray? The one who goes astray from the right is lost. Who is a straight man? The one who speaks the truth is straight. Straighten your word, daughter, and straighten your heart. What is right stands.

Lord, how shall I guard my brother? Guard your brother. Do not deceive him. If my brother deceives me, shall I kill him? Do not kill your brother. Ask him, and listen to his word. I shall ask my brother. If he asks me for cattle, what shall I give him? Give him half of them. Two brothers are strong. A brother is dear to a brother.

Great one, who eats the grain? The one who ploughs the field, he eats the grain. And who does not eat the grain? The one who does not work, he does not eat. Who receives the wage? The one who works, he receives the wage. Who becomes rich in livestock? The one who works, he becomes rich in livestock. Who draws the plough? The bull draws the plough. When one ploughs the field, the earth gives him grain. If one does not plough, the earth gives nothing.

Lord, who is a good king? The king is a shepherd of men. What does the shepherd do? He guards the sheep from the wolf. When a wolf arrives at the sheep, the dog and the shepherd drive it away. And who is the king's wolf? His wolf is the one who deceives. The ill-minded king devours his own sheep. The sheep flee from him. What is the wolf's plunder? The wolf's plunder is the lamb and the piglet. When the shepherd guards the sheep, the sheep live.

When a man dies, famous one, what lives? His name lives, and his fame lives. And where is he gone? He is gone. The fire burns him. Does it burn his fame? It does not burn his fame. Is there rest for him? There is rest for him. Who remembers him? His sons remember him. They hear his fame. He goes away; his fame stands.

Great one, who wins fame? The hero wins fame. And where does he win it? In war he wins it. Where does the hero with good horses go? He goes to war. Does he die? In war he dies, and his fame stands. Whose fame is imperishable? The one who slew the serpent, his fame is imperishable. Where do men hear it? On the broad earth they hear it. I shall slay the serpent! Be strong, and do what is right. May your fame be good.

Where do those who die go? A deep water lies yonder. Two dogs guard the crossing. In what do they go? They go in a boat. What do they carry? They carry nothing. Do they come back? No one comes back from yonder. Do they see the sun? They do not see it. Lord, I am afraid. Do not tremble in fear, dear one. The living see the light.

Great one, to whom does death come? Death comes to the cattle. She comes to brothers. She comes to us. And what does not die? Fame does not die. Which fame lives? Good fame lives. Is the ill-famed man lost? He is lost. Remember, dear friend: good fame stands.

Lord, what is sleep? Sleep is the brother of death. Does a man die in sleep? He does not die, and he wakes up. The one who is gone, he does not wake up. Where does the mind go in sleep? The mind goes yonder, and it comes back. And in death, where does the mind go? In death it goes yonder, and it does not come back. Do not tremble in fear of sleep, daughter. When it dawns, you will wake up.

Lord, who sets a man's name? The father sets a famous name for the son and the daughter. When he is gone, who carries it? The sons carry it. Is it lost? The one who deceives, his name is lost. The one who speaks the truth, men hear his fame. Guard your name, daughter. The name of the father dwells in the son.

Great one, what is a race? A race is the sons of the fathers. The one who is born in a famous race, he carries a famous name. What is the offspring of a dog? The offspring of a dog is a dog, and the offspring of a horse is a horse. Does he become good through his name? Through his mind he becomes good. Where are the fathers gone? They are gone. The name comes from them; fame is one's own.

Famous one, what is fame? Fame is that which men hear. Who listens to fame? The gods listen to fame, and we listen to it. Who speaks the hero's fame? The one who knows the words, he speaks it. If no one speaks it, it does not go. Then I shall learn the words. Learn them, and speak the truth.

Who creates the word? The one who knows, he creates it. And what does the carpenter build? The carpenter builds a wheel. From the tree he builds it. And from what does the one who knows create it? He creates it from the heart and the mind. With what does he put them in order? He puts them in order with the mouth. The wheel is swift, and the word is swift. A broken wheel does not go. A broken word does not stand. Daughter, put your words in order.

Lord, who gave you the word? The gods gave me the word. Where did they put it? They put it in my mouth and in my heart. Do they give it to many? They do not give it to many. The one whom the gods have come to love, to him they give it. Have they come to love me? I do not know. Call upon the gods, and listen. When they have given it to you, you will know. The gift of the gods is great.

Where is the word born? In the heart it is born, and in the mind it grows. The mouth does not create the word. The mouth conveys it. Where does the word go from the heart? It goes to the mouth, and from the mouth it goes out to men. That which is not born in the heart is a lie. How shall my heart become straight? Dear one, listen, and learn. A good word is born in a good heart.

Great one, I heard the one of good words. What does he create? He creates fame. Of whom does he create fame? The one who slew the serpent, of him he creates fame. What does he receive? He receives a reward. Who gives it? The king gives the reward. When he hears the fame, the king becomes joyful. What is the reward? The reward is silver and a garment. The reward goes away; fame stands.

What does the driver yoke? The driver yokes the swift horses to the chariot. What do the horses draw? The horses draw the chariot. And what does the one of good words yoke? He yokes the words. To what does he yoke them? He yokes them to the mind. The mind is the driver of them. Who breaks the wheel? An ill-minded driver breaks the wheel. Dear friend, yoke your words, and drive them.

How shall I learn the words? Son, listen, and ask. Whom shall I hear? The one who knows, listen to him. What shall I seek? Seek the true word. Where shall I seek him? Seek him in his household. When I have heard them, what shall I do? Remember them. The one who hears well, he learns them. The one who works, he learns.

If no one hears a word, does it live? It does not live. The one who has heard it, in him it dwells. Who hears well? The one who listens, he hears well. The one who speaks, and the one who hears: these two create fame. Speak, and let us hear.

Is the word first, or the thought? The thought is first. Where does the thought lie? In the mind it lies. Then the word comes. Let not your mouth run ahead. Let the mind drive it. When a word has gone from my mouth, what shall I do? That which has gone does not come back. Remember, son. Then speak.
